case_title: Sanjay Raghunath Agarwal v. The Directorate of Enforcement
statutory_provisions: IPC ss.406, 407, 415 to 420, 120B r/w s.34 (predicate FIR offences); PMLA s.3 (money-laundering, alleged), s.4 (punishment referred to)
aggravating_circumstances: None noted by the court; prosecution alleged the appellant was the kingpin and mastermind (alleged only)
mitigating_circumstances: None noted by the court; defence argued the appellant offered only professional services (argument only)
trial_court_outcome: No trial verdict stated; Metropolitan Sessions Judge remanded the appellant to judicial custody on 27.09.2022
neutral_facts: A company's managing director lodged a complaint alleging that the company engaged the accused to raise Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) worth about USD 71.09 million (INR 318 crore), but only about USD 0.4 million (INR 2.20 crore) was transferred to the company. The complaint alleged the balance was misappropriated by forging signatures on pledged documents. An FIR was registered in 2013 under criminal breach of trust, cheating and conspiracy provisions, following a magistrate's order. A securities regulator later found that persons had misled investors through a series of identical GDR issues. Subsequently, an information report under the money-laundering law was recorded in 2022 naming several individuals and entities. The prosecution alleged that a subscribing entity financed by a bank loan subscribed to the GDRs, that the proceeds were held as collateral, and that only part of the loan repayment released funds to the company, causing a loss of about USD 15.60 million. The GDRs were later converted into shares and sold in the domestic market. It was alleged that the accused, a chartered accountant, advised the company on the offering, coordinated the listing, provided formats for board resolutions, and helped transfer funds from the company's bank account to a foreign subsidiary. It was further alleged that the accused knew of an arrangement to share the GDR proceeds and withheld the subscriber list from the stock exchange. The accused was arrested in September 2022 on these allegations.
number_of_offences: 11 charged (10 IPC sections in the predicate FIR: ss.406, 407, 415, 416, 417, 418, 419, 420, 120B, 34; plus PMLA s.3 alleged); 0 finally upheld (no conviction; bail granted)
financial_property_loss: Alleged loss of USD 15.60 million to Farmax (alleged by prosecution; not decided by court)
premeditation_planning: Not found by the court; prosecution alleged deliberate planning and concealment of the subscriber list (alleged)
motive: alleged: sharing of GDR proceeds under an arrangement between a co-accused and the company promoters
key_evidence_accepted: No trial evidence assessed. The court accepted as undisputed that the ECIR and prosecution complaint followed the 2013 FIR and SEBI's 2020 order, and that no final report was filed in the predicate FIR.
post_offence_conduct: Not stated as conduct; prosecution apprehended flight risk, which the court said could be addressed by conditions
custody_duration: In custody from 26.09.2022 (arrest) until the Supreme Court's bail order; total period not stated
bail_history: High Court judgment dated 07.12.2022 in CRLP No. 9695 of 2022 (bail-related outcome not stated); Supreme Court granted bail
legal_representation: Appellant: R. Basant, Senior Advocate, with others. Respondent (Directorate of Enforcement): S.V. Raju, Additional Solicitor General, with others.
investigation_status: FIR registered 2013; no final report filed in predicate FIR; ECIR lodged 05.05.2022; appellant arrested 26.09.2022; prosecution complaint filed under PMLA ss.44 and 45
procedural_irregularity: Court noted no final report filed in the predicate FIR for about nine years; no other lapse noted
appeal_history: Trial level: appellant remanded to judicial custody on 27.09.2022 (no verdict). High Court: judgment dated 07.12.2022, outcome not stated. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, appellant enlarged on bail.
prosecution_argument: Appellant is the kingpin and mastermind of the transactions; bail should be refused under the twin conditions of s.45 PMLA; the appellant is a flight risk
defence_argument: Prolonged custody without charge-sheet in predicate offence for over nine years; de facto complainant was sought to be arrested but remand was rejected; appellant is a chartered accountant who offered only professional services; no material shows possession of proceeds of crime
legal_principle_applied: Bail under s.45(1) PMLA: where the prosecution complaint gives room for a valid argument that the second condition in s.45(1)(ii) is satisfied, continued incarceration is not justified; flight-risk concerns are met by imposing conditions
judicial_mitigating_factors: None expressly weighed as mitigating; court relied on the absence of a final report in the predicate FIR and the appellant's continued incarceration
other_sentence_order: Bail subject to conditions set by the Special Court, including surrender of passport and regular appearance before the Special Court whenever the prosecution complaint is posted
